question: The equations $3x+2y=7$ and $x+y=3$ are represented by $AX=B$. Use $X=A^{-1}B$ to determine $x-y$.
explanation:
Step 1: Form the matrices
We have $$A=\begin{bmatrix}3&2\\1&1\end{bmatrix},\quad X=\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\end{bmatrix},\quad B=\begin{bmatrix}7\\3\end{bmatrix}$$
Step 2: Calculate the inverse
Since $|A|=3-2=1$, $$A^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}1&-2\\-1&3\end{bmatrix}$$
Step 3: Find the variables
Therefore, $$X=A^{-1}B=\begin{bmatrix}1&-2\\-1&3\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}7\\3\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}1\\2\end{bmatrix}$$ Thus, $x=1$ and $y=2$.
Step 4: Calculate the requested value
Hence, $$x-y=1-2=-1$$
